Privacy Policy

Last updated: 3 November 2026

VS Developers (“we”, “us”, “our”) respects your privacy. This policy explains what personal information we collect through this website, how we use it and the choices you have.

1. Information we collect

We collect only the information you choose to share when you enquire about our plotted developments:

  • Your name, phone number and email address (email is optional).
  • The project you are interested in, the type of help you need and any message you write.
  • Basic technical information that your browser shares automatically when you visit any website, such as device type and browser.

2. How the enquiry forms work

The enquiry forms on this website do not save your details in a website database. When you submit a form, it opens WhatsApp with your message prepared so that you can review and send it to us. Once you send the message, it is handled through WhatsApp and is also subject to WhatsApp’s own terms and privacy policy.

3. How we use your information

  • To respond to your enquiry, share project details and arrange site visits.
  • To help with documentation, registration and home-loan assistance when you ask for these services.
  • To keep records of our communication with you and to improve our service.
  • To meet legal and regulatory obligations.

4. Sharing of information

We do not sell your personal information. We may share it only with people who help us serve you, such as legal advisers, banks or financial institutions you ask us to coordinate with, and with authorities where the law requires it.

5. Cookies and third-party services

This website does not use advertising or tracking cookies of its own. Fonts are loaded from Google Fonts, which may receive technical information such as your IP address. Links such as WhatsApp, phone and email open third-party apps that follow their own policies.

6. Retention and security

We keep your enquiry details only for as long as needed to respond to you, to complete any transaction you enter into, and to meet legal requirements. We take reasonable steps to protect the information we hold, but no method of transmission or storage is completely secure.

7. Your choices and rights

Subject to applicable Indian law, including the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, you may ask us to confirm the information we hold about you, correct it, or delete it, and you may withdraw your consent to be contacted at any time. Please write to us using the details below.

8. Children

This website is meant for adults interested in property. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children.

9. Changes to this policy

We may update this policy from time to time. The latest version will always be available on this page with its date of update.

Refund & Cancellation Policy

Last updated: 3 November 2026

This policy explains how cancellations and refunds are handled for bookings made with VS Developers. It is a general summary. If your signed booking form or agreement says something different, that document applies.

1. Who this policy covers

This policy applies to booking amounts, token advances and other payments made to VS Developers for a plot in any of our plotted developments before a sale deed is registered in your favour.

2. Booking

A booking is confirmed only when we issue a written receipt and the booking documents are completed. Please keep every receipt and ask us for a copy of the terms before you pay.

3. Cancelling a booking

  • Send your cancellation request in writing to our email address or office address given below.
  • The request is treated as received on the date we receive it. Verbal requests are not accepted.
  • Any deduction or retention from the amount paid, and the time within which a refund is made, will be as stated in your booking form or agreement.

4. How refunds are made

Refunds that are due are paid by traceable banking channels to the person who made the payment, after we verify the request and the original receipts. We will confirm to you in writing when the refund is processed.

5. Cancellation by VS Developers

If we are unable to proceed with a booking, for example because the plot is no longer available or a legal or approval matter prevents the sale, we will inform you in writing and refund the amounts you paid in line with your booking documents.

6. After registration

Once a sale deed has been registered, the transaction is governed by the sale deed and applicable law, and the cancellation and refund steps in this policy no longer apply.

7. Questions or disputes

If you have a concern about a cancellation or refund, please contact us first so that we can try to resolve it quickly and fairly.

Buying guide

A simple checklist before you buy a residential plot

5 min read

Buying a plot is one of the biggest decisions a family makes. A calm, step-by-step approach makes it far easier.

1. Visit the site in person

Photos help, but a visit tells you more. Check how you reach the layout, the width and condition of internal roads, the surroundings, and whether the plot boundaries are clearly marked.

2. Ask about approvals

Ask whether the land has been converted for residential use and whether the layout has been approved by the competent authority. Request copies rather than relying on verbal assurance.

3. Check the basics of the layout

  • Roads, street lighting, drainage and sewage arrangements.
  • Water and power connections, or the plan to provide them.
  • Plot size, shape and the direction it faces.

4. Review the paperwork with a legal adviser

Share the documents with an independent lawyer of your choice and ask for their opinion before you commit.

5. Understand the full cost

Along with the plot price, plan for stamp duty, registration charges and any other costs mentioned in the agreement. Ask for everything in writing.

6. Pay safely and keep records

Make payments through traceable banking channels, collect a receipt for every payment and read the agreement fully before you sign.

This article is general information and not legal advice.

Approvals

DC conversion and layout approval, explained simply

4 min read

You will often hear that a plot is “DC converted” or “approved”. Here is what these phrases generally mean in Karnataka.

What is DC conversion?

Land that is recorded for agricultural use has to be converted to non-agricultural use before it can be used for a residential layout. In Karnataka this conversion is granted through an order from the Deputy Commissioner (DC) of the district.

What is layout approval?

Separate from conversion, a residential layout generally needs approval of its plan from the competent planning authority. The approved plan shows the plots, roads and common areas.

Why both matter

Conversion shows the land can be used for housing, and an approved layout plan shows how the land is divided. Together they help you confirm that the plot you are buying is part of a properly planned layout.

What you can ask for

  • A copy of the conversion order and the survey number it refers to.
  • A copy of the approved layout plan.
  • The plot number and dimensions as shown on that plan.

Match the documents to the plot

Check that the survey number, plot number and measurements in the documents match the plot you were shown on site. Your legal adviser can help you confirm this.

This article is general information and not legal advice. Rules and procedures can change, so please verify the latest requirements.

Documents

Documents to verify before registering a plot

5 min read

Clear paperwork is the foundation of a worry-free purchase. These are the records most buyers ask to see.

Ownership records

  • The previous sale deeds that show how the seller came to own the land.
  • The RTC (Record of Rights, Tenancy and Crops) extract for the land.

Encumbrance certificate

An encumbrance certificate shows whether the property has registered loans or other claims against it. Ask your lawyer for how many years it should cover.

Conversion and layout approvals

The conversion order and the approved layout plan show that the land can be used for housing and how the plots are laid out.

Khata and tax records

Check the khata certificate and extract, and the receipts for property or land tax paid up to date.

Agreement and registration

  • Read the agreement for sale carefully, including payment schedule and timelines.
  • Confirm that the sale deed is registered at the sub-registrar’s office in your name.

This article is general information and not legal advice. Please consult a qualified lawyer for your specific purchase.

Planning

Plot or apartment: which suits your plans?

4 min read

Both choices can be right. The better one is the one that fits your family, budget and timeline.

Freedom to design

With a plot you decide the design, the number of floors, the layout of rooms and the garden. With an apartment, the design is fixed by the builder.

Time and effort

Building a home on a plot takes planning, approvals for construction and time to manage the work. An apartment can be simpler if you want to move in sooner.

Cost and budget

A plot lets you spread spending across two stages, buying the land first and building later when you are ready. Ask lenders about options for both the plot and the construction.

Upkeep and community

Apartments usually come with shared amenities and maintenance charges. Plotted communities offer more space and privacy, and you take care of your own home.

A long-term view

Land is a long-term asset, but no property gives guaranteed returns. Choose a location you are comfortable with and verify every document before you decide.
